idiom_name: Sidekiq job class (perform_async) or ActiveJob perform_later with a JSON job hash
implementation_notes: A command message in Ruby is a job: MyJob.perform_async(args) serializes the worker class name plus arguments into a JSON hash ({class, args, jid, queue, retry}) and pushes it to Redis, where a worker later constantizes the class and calls perform - the class name is the discriminator, the arguments are the payload, and routing, retries and the dead set come from the framework. ActiveJob's perform_later provides the same shape behind a queue-adapter abstraction (Sidekiq, Solid Queue, ...), which is the Rails-idiomatic layer to program against. A hand-rolled command bus (a Hash with a :type key dispatched by public_send) works in-process but loses durability, retries and visibility.
code_sketch:
class ReserveStockJob
  include Sidekiq::Job

  def perform(order_id, qty)
    Stock.reserve(order_id, qty)
  end
end

ReserveStockJob.perform_async(order_id, qty)   # command message on Redis
pitfalls: Arguments are JSON-encoded: symbols, Time objects and ActiveRecord instances either raise at enqueue time or silently degrade to strings/hashes - pass ids and plain values.
The class name is the wire contract and the arguments are positional: renaming the job or changing its arity breaks queued and retried jobs unless a versioned name or keyword-hash argument is used.
Jobs are retried by default (with the same arguments), so perform must be idempotent or guarded by a deduplication key.
